observation_summary: The compiler enters an infinite recursion (StackOverflowError) when processing recursive inheritance or interface implementation chains, specifically during type checking.
hypothesis: The type checking algorithm fails to detect cycles in the inheritance/implementation graph. When a type implements itself or forms a circular dependency, the recursive calls in 'isSubtype' and 'getImplementedInterfaces' continue indefinitely.
prediction: The fix will involve introducing a mechanism to track visited types during the traversal of the inheritance/implementation graph to detect and break cycles, likely using a Set or a similar structure to keep track of types already processed in the current recursion stack.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace shows deep recursion between 'PrototypeObjectType.isSubtype' and 'FunctionType.getImplementedInterfaces'. This is a classic symptom of an algorithm traversing a graph without cycle detection. The fix must modify the traversal logic to prevent infinite loops.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an algorithmic failure in the type-checking procedure. It lacks the necessary logic (cycle detection) to handle circular dependencies in the inheritance graph, leading to infinite recursion. This is a procedural/algorithmic flaw rather than a missing guard (Checking) or a simple value assignment error.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a check is missing, the root cause is the lack of a cycle-detection algorithm in a recursive traversal, which is more fundamental than a simple boundary or null check.
